p.i: Reipublicæ agatur, Magistratus omnes cordatos, non solum virium, sed etiam animi satis habituros ad jus potestatemque suam etiam me tacente defendendam. Satis quippe eos nos-se' agi hîc de summa rerum suarum, dum & melior ac nobilior pars potestatis ipsis eripitur, & hac erepta altera pars, quæ circa res civiles occupatur, nequaquam in tuto esse potest. Habet enim, secundum doctrinam Ecclesiarum Reformatarum omnium, Magistratus sceptrum duos veluti apices, potestatem nimirum Ecclesiasticam externam, non

page.notes: The "&" marks are printed as the italic ampersand-like sign, transcribed as &. "nos-se'" keeps the printed apostrophe after "se", which may be a printing error. "Habet" is read from a faint "bet" with an old-style e, so it is a likely reading and not checked letter by letter. The page number is not printed. The catchword "non" is at the lower right. A "Digitized by Google" watermark at the bottom right is not transcribed.
